site.data_quality: LOLA GDR is a shape/radius map. Its label states gridding used surface interpolation in higher-resolution regions. Product does not supply a per-pixel confidence layer; measurement uncertainty is therefore unquantified.

data_coverage.note: Direct-shot coverage is not quantified by the LOLA GDR product.

checks.name: slope_p90
checks.basis: Reference only: a draft NASA VIPER requirement limits lander effective slope to 10°. This 926 m slope percentile is not the foot-scale effective-slope test.

checks.name: median_local_relief_3x3
checks.basis: 60 m at 1.39 km scale is a research assumption; no vehicle-specific limit is validated.

mission_suitability.qualification: Provisional terrain-only screening; criteria are configurable research assumptions, not validated vehicle or site-certification limits.

ranking_method: Weighted mean of exp(-absolute difference / variable tolerance), normalized across available same-unit variables at matching scales.

candidate_coverage.note: Ranks only Earth DEM product contexts ingested here; this is not global search or a new-analogue determination.

limitations: Terrain similarity is not probability, analogue validation, or site suitability.
LOLA LDEM_64 is a gridded shape/radius product; interpolation was used, and direct-observation coverage is not quantified in this crop.

MOLA MEG128 comparison uses observed-bin elevation range over the 10.19 km footprint as a regional-relief proxy; it does not estimate slope or roughness, and sparse count-grid support can miss local extrema.
Copernicus GLO-30 is a surface model with different acquisition and processing characteristics.
Contexts are resampled to 463.06 m cells over about 10.19 km, but scales and uncertainties still differ.
Mission thresholds are provisional research-screening assumptions documented in the methodology; they are not validated against a specific vehicle or engineering design.

A Moon-only Diviner nighttime regolith-temperature context is exposed where available but is not paired with Earth thermal data or scored. Mars sites also expose generalized USGS map-unit codes; these are not local material measurements. Mineralogy, radiation, illumination, and volatiles are not included.
